QUANTUM SENSING WITHOUT CALIBRATING THE NOISE AXIS
A finite controller based on returning error trajectories
1 November 2026 (Australia/Brisbane)

Research status
===============
This investigation derives a physical-model construction, ordinary proofs, and
independent executable checks. Historical novelty, laboratory realization, and
practical superiority over the strongest conventional methods are unestablished.
The main result includes continuing sensor noise during finite meter interaction,
feedback latency, readout and reset. It allows constant classical report errors.
Protected reference memory, specified coherent interactions, and a shared static
native noise axis remain material premises. Generic quantum controller faults
are separately charged; this is not a fault-tolerance threshold theorem.

The initial scientific objective was a quantum sensor whose improving precision
does not demand equally improving knowledge of an environmental noise direction.
The strongest ordinary known-noise QEC constructions were considered first.
Their failure with a nuisance noise direction identified the opening. The useful
result changes the physical operation set by allowing scalar reservoir-rate
control. That operation is neither free information nor an ordinary Pauli pulse.

1. Task and exact physical contract
==================================
There is one sensing qubit S with unknown frequency omega and one protected
reference qubit A. Z|0>=|0>, Z|1>=-|1>. Encode a logical qubit by

    |0_L>=|0_S 0_A>,    |1_L>=|1_S 1_A>.

Its input can be unknown and entangled with an arbitrary untouched reference R.
For the final sensing task the input is |+_L>. The sensor has Hamiltonian
H_omega=omega Z_S/2 and Markov noise

    L_theta=sqrt(gamma) J_theta,
    J_theta=cos(theta) X_S+sin(theta) Y_S.

The azimuth theta is unknown, constant, and common to every native-rate setting.
Two strictly positive rates gamma_l<gamma_h can be selected. The physical control
changes only this scalar coefficient. It does not turn off the noise, resolve
theta, add an independently oriented noise source, or alter H_omega. A microscopic
resource consistent with this contract is a tunable scalar coupling to one fixed
system operator J_theta and a sufficiently broad stationary Markov reservoir.
Its laboratory synthesis and Markov approximation are not supplied by the theorem.

source_excerpts.text:
Deferred classical readout of the meter's logical Pauli frame
1 November 2026

Claim audited. In the finite-meter construction, the coherent CZ from logical
ancilla A to meter M may be omitted, if the true final meter Z outcome can be
decoded later with a sufficiently small total classical error. The first noisy
readout can still drive the native-rate feedback immediately. Accurate live
logical-frame information is unnecessary.

1. Exact frame identity

For a fixed sensor-jump path and logical Z_A label z=+/-1, the active meter
state before erasure is
  cos(Phi)|0>_M - i z sin(Phi)|1>_M,
where Phi is path dependent but independent of z. A projective QND Z_M outcome
m=0 or 1 therefore induces, on the logical state,
  scalar(path,m) Z_A^m.
The scalar may carry a path-dependent global phase but no logical-label
dependence. This is precisely the frame removed by the earlier coherent CZ.

Z_A commutes with the signal Hamiltonian omega Z_S/2, the native sensor jumps
cos(theta)X_S+sin(theta)Y_S, and all later meter interactions of the form
g_S Z_S X_M + g_A Z_A X_M. It also commutes with later meter measurements.
Thus after M meter outcomes the only change from the coherently erased
construction is Z_A^B, B=sum_i m_i modulo 2. All meter outcome probabilities,
including joint correlations with syndrome paths and the first noisy live
report, remain identical. The parent's finite controller transfer matrix and
its drift formula are unchanged.

The final sensing observable
  O=(X_S Y_A+Y_S X_A)/2
anticommutes with Z_A. Its sampled product outcome z_final must therefore be
multiplied by (-1)^B. No physical recovery pulse is needed.

2. Delayed readout and its resource cost

Assume each measured meter remains in its true classical Z eigenstate while
it is read repeatedly. Given the bit, the L reports have independent error
probabilities bounded by (1-eta_r)/2, with eta_r>0. A majority decoder obeys
  P(m_hat!=m) <= exp(-L eta_r^2/2).
For at most M meter uses and a total frame-error budget alpha_frame, it suffices
to take an odd L with
  L >= (2/eta_r^2)log(M/alpha_frame).
The union bound gives P(any decoded bit wrong)<=alpha_frame. This remains valid
under adaptive sensor control because the conditional per-bit bound is uniform
over the history. Requiring every bit correct is sufficient, though not optimal
for decoding only their parity.

PRIMARY SOURCES AND ACTUAL DEPENDENCIES
Research cutoff: 1 November 2026, Australia/Brisbane.

No claim of historical novelty is made. The core identities, controller,
finite-time reduction and estimator are derived in the accompanying proofs.
The sources below define strong competitors and established machinery.

1. S. Zhou, M. Zhang, J. Preskill and L. Jiang,
   Achieving the Heisenberg limit in quantum metrology using quantum error correction,
   Nature Communications9,78 (2018).
   https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-017-02510-3
   https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5758555/
   Governing scope: finite-dimensional Markov model, HNLS condition, noiseless
   ancillas and arbitrarily fast accurate control. Strong known-noise construction.
   It does not supply unknown static-axis calibration or the new finite detector.

2. R. Demkowicz-Dobrzanski, J. Czajkowski and P. Sekatski,
   Adaptive Quantum Metrology under General Markovian Noise,
   Physical Review X7,041009 (2017).
   https://journals.aps.org/prx/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevX.7.041009
   https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.06280
   Established adaptive-channel precision-bound framework. Our exact finite
   nuisance-path proof is an application/refinement, not a claim to invent it.

3. F. Albarelli and R. Demkowicz-Dobrzanski,
   Probe Incompatibility in Multiparameter Noisy Quantum Metrology,
   Physical Review X12,011039 (2022).
   https://journals.aps.org/prx/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevX.12.011039
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.11264
   Strong adaptive, entanglement-assisted multiparameter bounds, including
   simultaneous unitary/noise parameters. Constrains novelty of nuisance geometry.

4. E. Abbasgholinejad et al.,
   Error-corrected function estimation advantage in multiparameter Hamiltonians,
   arXiv:2609.16226 (September2026).
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16226
   Full HTML read at https://arxiv.org/html/2609.16226v1
   Functional HNLS, Hamiltonian nuisance removal and tight SQL/HL results. The
   present nuisance instead parameterizes a jump orientation. Unknown-parameter
   function estimation itself is already established work.

5. Q. Liu and S. Zhou,
   Subsystem Quantum Error Correction for Noisy Quantum Metrology,
   arXiv:2606.19628 (June2026).
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19628
   Full HTML read at https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19628v1
   Specified Pauli error operators; local estimation w
